```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse  = TRUE,
  comment   = "#>",
  fig.path = "../man/figures/",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 5
)

scc_available <- nchar(Sys.which("scc")) > 0L
rlang_path <- system.file("pkgs/rlang", package = "glockr")
```

```{r library}
library(glockr)
```

## Counting by file

`scc_by_file()` expands results to one row per source file, adding `filename`,
`location`, and logical flags for `generated` and `minified` files.

```{r scc-by-file, eval = FALSE}
scc_by_file(rlang_path)
#> # A tibble: 383 × 12
#>    language filename     location lines  code comments
#>    <chr>    <chr>        <chr>    <int> <int>    <int>
#>  1 R        sink.R       /Users/…     8     6        1
#>  2 R        testthat.R   /Users/…     7     4        1
#>  3 R        test-obj.R   /Users/…     5     5        0
#>  4 R        c-lib.R      /Users/…   413   312       26
#>  5 R        test-friend… /Users/…   299   283        1
#>  6 R        nse-inject.R /Users/…   551    63      472
#>  7 R        aaa-topics.R /Users/…    93    65       10
#>  8 R        quo.R        /Users/…   752   394      298
#>  9 R        attr.R       /Users/…   302    72      211
#> 10 R        test-standa… /Users/…    32    27        0
#> # ℹ 373 more rows
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: blanks <int>,
#> #   complexity <int>, weighted_complexity <dbl>,
#> #   bytes <int>, generated <lgl>, minified <lgl>
```

Filter to just the R source files and sort by complexity:

```{r scc-by-file-r, eval = FALSE}
r_files <- scc_by_file(rlang_path, include_ext = "r")
r_files_sub <- r_files[, c("filename", "lines", "code", "comments", "blanks", "complexity")]
r_files_sub[order(r_files_sub$complexity, decreasing = TRUE), ]
#> # A tibble: 163 × 6
#>    filename              lines  code comments blanks complexity
#>    <chr>                 <int> <int>    <int>  <int>      <int>
#>  1 cnd-abort.R            1561   691      729    141        152
#>  2 standalone-cli.R        653   432      172     49        135
#>  3 trace.R                1170   807      188    175        134
#>  4 deparse.R              1092   819      114    159        111
#>  5 standalone-vctrs.R      669   505       48    116        107
#>  6 call.R                 1076   451      550     75         92
#>  7 standalone-obj-type.R   313   206       72     35         64
#>  8 cnd-entrace.R           405   213      147     45         61
#>  9 utils.R                 372   302       11     59         59
#> 10 expr.R                  421   157      237     27         52
#> # ℹ 153 more rows
```

## Visualizing file composition

With `ggplot2` and `tidyr` we can plot the code / comment / blank split for
the most complex R source files.

```{r plot, eval = scc_available}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

r_files <- scc_by_file(rlang_path, include_ext = "r")

# keep the 15 files with the most lines
top15 <- r_files[order(r_files$lines, decreasing = TRUE), ][1:15, ]

long <- pivot_longer(
  top15,
  cols      = c(code, comments, blanks),
  names_to  = "type",
  values_to = "n_lines"
)
long$type <- factor(long$type, levels = c("blanks", "comments", "code"))

ggplot(long, aes(x = n_lines, y = reorder(filename, n_lines), fill = type)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(code = "#2166ac", comments = "#92c5de", blanks = "#d1e5f0"),
    labels = c(code = "Code", comments = "Comments", blanks = "Blanks")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "rlang R source — line composition (top 15 by lines)",
    x     = "Lines",
    y     = NULL,
    fill  = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
